text:
alex_sales: ACME POC: their app gets 403 invalid_org when calling /v1/generate with the key we issued. They say they set org header matching their org. Anyone seen this?

jamie_se: :eyes: can you paste the curl and full error body?

alex_sales: curl command:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123\" \\
     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
     -d '{\"model\":\"rwk-large\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' \\
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response:
{"error":"invalid_org","message":"Key bound to org redwood-test, request org acme-inc"}

mohit_engineer: sounds like token was created under our test org. For POC we often need the key to be org-bound to acme-inc or use tenant header. Do they set x-redwood-org?

alex_sales: They said they set `x-org-id: acme-inc` in their proxy. Not sure if we require `x-redwood-org`. Any internal check?

mohit_engineer: Our auth layer looks for either `x-redwood-org` or `x-org-id` mapping to the project tenant id. For legacy tokens we also check `org` claim in JWT. Quick test — could they try adding header `x-redwood-org: acme-inc`?

eze_support: short-term fix: create a temporary API key explicitly bound to acme-inc via Console -> Keys -> Create -> Bind tenant: acme-inc. Then give them the new key. Long-term: if we expect them to use proxy, update the mapping in the edge to accept `x-org-id`. I'll create a temporary key now.

ci-bot: created key sk_temp_acme_789 bound to org acme-inc (expires in 7 days). :lock: 

alex_sales: forwarding sk_temp_acme_789, they tested — :thumbsup: 200 OK, generation working. Acme asked about production plan for key rotation and least privilege.

mohit_engineer: recommend short TTL keys for POC, and use project-scoped scopes like `inference:invoke`. For prod we can set up org-to-project binding and SSO-based service accounts.

eze_support: I'll add notes to the support ticket about rotation and a checklist: 1) bind keys to org, 2) set `x-redwood-org` header when proxy-ing, 3) create SVC account for long lived access.

alex_sales: great. Closing the swarm. Thanks all. :tada:
